images.caption: Figure 2:Inference pipeline and latency profiling for one autoregressive generation.State-of-the-art few-step autoregressive video diffusion models generate each new frame by first updating the KV cache using the previous frame’s denoised latent (𝒛0i−1{\bm{z}}^{i-1}_{0}) through a DiT evaluation, then performing multiple denoising steps followed by VAE decoding. The color gradient of the model components denotes speed: from white (fastest operations) to red (slowest).(a)The fastest baseline, Causal Forcing++(Zhao et al., 2026a), takes 271 ms to generate a frame at 480p but only 30% of wall time is spent on diffusion sampling.(b)FastFramesreduces latency nearly 8× by replacing the non-denoising “accessories” with lightweight alternatives and performing systems-level optimizations to speed up each DiT evaluation.

Figure 3:Comparing pixel decoders.Our pixel decoder (right) renders thin structures and details like hair and raindrops while being two orders of magnitude faster than Wan’s VAE (left). A single linear projection (middle) cannot render sharp outputs, but is sufficient for recognizing the scene and suggests that pixel rendering does not require an expensive decoder.

Figure 4:Qualitative comparisons.We compareFastFrames-S with Causal Forcing++ at 1.3B parameters andFastFrames-L with Krea-Realtime at 14B. Each example shows frames at00and55seconds.FastFrames-S achieves comparable visual sharpness to Causal Forcing++, such as the details in the sculpture (first example) and leaves (second example), while being nearly 8× faster.FastFrames-L achieves comparable visual realism to Krea-Realtime, including composition of “paper origami dragon” (third), and legible text of “stay curious” (fourth) while being 10× faster.
See ourwebsitefor video playback.

Figure 5:Interactive generation and latency results.Left: example of interaction with LingBot’s official implementation vs. withFastFramesoptimizations. Given a single keypress,FastFramesis 16× faster to respond.
Right: generation latency of officially released implementations and our optimized implementations.
We measure steady-state latency on NVIDIA B200 GPUs at 832×480 resolution with a full KV cache and include distributed optimizations such as Ulysses where officially supported.
Times include diffusion sampling (four steps for LingBot and three for RealWonder), action conditioning, KV-cache updates, and pixel decoding.
Our optimizations provide speedups of 3× to 22×. See theproject websitefor the video demonstration.

images.caption: Figure 6:KV refinement ablation.Autoregressive baselines refine the KV cache using an additional DiT evaluation, which is costly but effective. Removing that refinement naively (third column) substantially degrades the scene’s consistency; the objects in the scenes change over time. Even training without the refinement (fourth column) does not fix the problem. Either the subject changes over time (the face changes in the second example), or noticeable artifacts appear (clothing in the first example, fingers in the second example). Our KV refinement network (second column) replaces the DiT evaluation and performs equally while being an order of magnitude faster.
